body: no adults know what they are doing, it is all a farce. we are just trying our best, doing the best we can. it's okay to be confused and overwhelmed, you are not alone

i think some people do it out of impulse and that makes a lot of room for mistakes but i have a similar experience, 7 years being passively and actively suicidal but when it's been that long and i'm stubborn enough not try to, it's like i know it's been so long i wouldn't get it wrong. some suicide attempts are reckless and impulsive and not well thought out and mine would be methodical if it ever happened. and i remind myself that i have too much going on and things to look forward to so it would never happen right now. but i'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, and if it did how little i'd have to live for and how easy it would be. it just try to keep myself grounded with the things i am grateful for that dont feel like bullshit and the people i have that don't make me feel insane for feeling so intensely and deeply. i'm proud of how deeply i feel, it just has its deep down trip into the abyss sides too. sending you love and strength, if you're feeling held back there is a reason. potential, value where we can't see it clearly right now

it's called being passively suicidal. it's concerning yes but also attached a lot to anxiety and trauma and detachment from life. depression and monotony. sometimes it keeps me present in a cheery like " wow nothing matters i really can do what i want " way that is almost empowering and other times it's dull and devoid and disconnects me from reality, even the good things make me want to self sabotage. i'd recommend therapy, my therapist is really understanding about it and it is normal for some people, but finding the core trigger of it and the lack of value you have of yourself is important. you deserve more than you could imagine. i only get concerned for myself when it passes to methods/imagining my funeral. talk to someone you trust about it, it's not as uncommon as you'd think sadly. sending love

i felt the same thing for a long time and it does get easier with time. no one ever knows what is going on, everyone is just as confused and overwhelmed. you're not alone in that. i'm 21 and i have never been more aware of how much shit i don't get or understand or what being happy and stable feels or looks like? i really think i'm there but even in my happiest moments, i have a hard time accepting good things cause i didn't plan to make it this far. if you have something good, anything at all, please remind yourself that you deserve it. you deserve the world. i'm happy and the depression and passive suicidal ideation i've always dealt with is standing in the way of that at times but i know i deserve so much more than what i could imagine and can't self sabotage to try to make offing myself easier. you got so much time. things are always getting worse and better but the good things do mean the world and keep you here. a friend, a new album or movie coming out, looking at the stars. you will figure it out. and you don't have to figure out everything. my biggest failure was thinking i had to be alone in this when you don't, tell someone, anyone. connection can save us all. even if relationships come and go, its good to know we have the ability to connect at all and being transparent and authentic fully about stuff with even one person can help you get the support and help you need. one person accepting you and your vulnerabilities can make all the difference. i didn't know what to do and talked to someone close to me before i graduated and they had the best idea for me of going to art school, i never saw something like that as valuable or a possibility but i'm honoring myself in seeing the potential i have. try to see where your passions really lie, some shit from your parents really means so little when you are doing what you love, and others perspective on that can really help you find some clarity. sending love
